title: EverythingStar playlist
description: A playlist document: the index a jukebox lists and a band is offered from. ADVISORY ONLY — the game's reader (src/lib/game/playlist.ts) is authoritative, and it is deliberately more tolerant than this schema: an unknown field is ignored, a broken song is skipped and named, and only a document with the wrong schemaVersion is refused whole. Use `bun run playlist:check <url>` to hold a document to that same reader. The wire contract is developers/playlist-api.md in this documentation.

schemaVersion.description: Exactly 1. A string "1" is not a version; a document with any other version is refused as a whole.

name.description: The name shown in the Playlists dialog.

description.description: A sentence about the playlist. Read but not yet shown on screen.

ondemand.description: Makes the document a search endpoint: it lists no songs by default and is asked again with the words in a query parameter. `true` uses ?q=…; an object names another parameter. A value that is neither leaves the document a catalogue.

param.description: The query-string parameter the source reads. A name that cannot be a parameter falls back to q and is reported as a problem.

onDemand.description: The spelling the reader also accepts. Use `ondemand` in a new document.

songs.description: The entries. Required for a catalogue; a capability may omit it, though "songs": [] is clearer.

song.description: One song's summary: enough to draw a row, chip it and offer it to a band, plus where its own document lives. The song document is the truth where the two disagree.

id.description: The song's key. Must be stable across edits and unique across every playlist: the library, the score board and the offline record are keyed by it.

title.description: Shown in the jukebox and filed under its first letter.

song.description: Where the song document lives, or a .sng package. Absolute, or relative to this playlist's own URL.

artist.description: A bare name, or an object. The object is preferred: an id keeps two artists with one name apart, and art gives the fallback cover something to show.

art.description: The cover. Falls back to the album's, then the artist's, then the song's initials. Resolved against this playlist's URL.

accent.description: A CSS colour for the fallback cover tile, e.g. #3fae5a.

durationMs.description: The song's length in milliseconds. 0 is accepted and shown as 0:00, but the list and the run's clock need the real value.

previewStartMs.description: Where the jukebox's preview starts when the song has no preview clip of its own.

offer.description: What a band can choose before the song document is fetched. It must agree with the song's own parts.

instruments.description: One entry per part, with the levels its charts carry. Lead and rhythm guitar are separate seats, so list both when the song says both. Do not put vocals here: the voice is its own field and a vocals entry is reported and skipped.

role.description: The part. A plain `guitar` is the fallback for a song with one guitar part.

difficulties.description: The levels this part's charts carry. An instrument with none is skipped with a problem, so leave it out instead.

voice.description: The words, or null/absent for an instrumental. `vocals` means the words carry pitch and are sung; `lyrics` means they carry none and are typed or read.

parts.description: 1 is a solo, 2 a duet, 3 a trio — the song's own fact, never a count of players. A fourth harmony is shared across the three.

video.description: A backdrop of the song's own. Omit it rather than send a video that cannot be embedded: the game falls back to the song's art, then its own artwork.

id.description: The YouTube video id, not a URL.

url.description: A direct video file. Resolved against this playlist's URL.
